title: In-universe correspondence & negotiation system (players ↔ GM/Claude via Journals)
summary: PCs write in-character messages to NPCs through Foundry Journals set up as a two-way messaging system; replies arrive the following session; players can use this to negotiate new equipment, mechs, or other requests. The exchange syncs to files, and the GM and Claude collaboratively write the responses and resulting new content together. Concretized further: writing is location-triggered (act at a place, or write what you wish had happened there), conversations run as a dialogue tree (pre-written multiple-choice branches, always with a final free-text option), off-script requests become an open ticket Claude answers with a best-shot SF2E-legal implementation (or one with interesting drawbacks), and the whole thing lives in Foundry Journals disguised via CSS as an in-fiction device.
description:
Surfaced as the answer to a narrower question about whether Frame class is a Directorate psych-profile verdict or player-chosen — the actual answer reframes the question: Frame builds (class, equipment, even the mech itself) are not fixed at character creation at all. Players can swap and upgrade over the campaign but aren't required to — some will use and upgrade the same mech for the entire campaign, others will actively seek out new mechs and equipment and push hard on what a Frame can become. Both are fine; the GM (and Claude) will balance requests as they come in rather than gating everything at creation.

The mechanism for this, and the actual pitch: in-character Journals set up like a messaging system, letting player characters write to other characters in-universe. Replies arrive the following session, not instantly — a deliberate asynchronous-correspondence pacing device, distinct from live table time. Players can use this channel to do things like negotiate new equipment or mechs, or pursue other in-fiction requests. That correspondence gets recorded and synced to files Claude can read, and the user and Claude then collaboratively write the new content (the reply, the new equipment, whatever the negotiation produces) together as the campaign moves forward.

This is a real, concrete validation of the harvest mechanism already designed in design/foundry-module-design.md §4 (GM-pulled promotable content, never automatic) — and it's closely related to, but more specific than, the already-tracked player-and-gm-journals-context-ingestion idea (private notes → context) and chat-log-knowledge-base (session events → structured data). This one is specifically a two-way, in-fiction, next-session-turnaround correspondence loop with concrete mechanical outcomes (new gear, new plot threads), not just note-taking.

**Mechanism, concretized in a follow-up message:** writing is location-triggered — a player at a given location (in-scene) can write what their character did there, or what they want to happen. The Frame-modification case is the flagship example: a PC might physically work on their own mech (spanner and wrench), but also coordinates with the crew responsible for rebuilding/maintaining it via an in-fiction comms device — that comms channel is the actual interface to the correspondence system for Frame changes. Conversations run as a **dialogue tree**: pre-written multiple-choice branches covering the obvious/anticipated ways an interaction goes (letting the GM and Claude pre-write and 'funnel' toward expected outcomes), but the **last option on any branch is always free-text** — the player can ask for anything. A free-text ask that falls outside what's pre-written becomes an **open ticket between the user and Claude**: Claude's job is to bring a best-shot implementation attempt that stays within SF2E's rules, or — if it can't cleanly — one with interesting, impactful drawbacks instead of just being refused. This is a standing process instruction for how these tickets get handled, not just flavor text (see also mission_statement.md in Claude's memory). Live, mid-session resolution is explicitly possible in principle ('characters can have interactions with NPCs even whilst sessions are ongoing') but the user expects all responses to happen between sessions at first — consistent with the async-now/OpenRouter-later split captured in character-creation-intake-form.

Storage: Foundry **Journals**, described as 'semi-secure' (exact permission model — player-private vs. GM-gated-until-resolved vs. something else — not yet specified), styled with custom **CSS to maintain the in-fiction illusion** that this is a comms device or terminal, not a raw journal entry. This is the same disguise-the-real-UI principle as terminal-login-landing-page (login/boot illusion) and probably shares visual language with in-scene-ui-panel-mimetic-controls (the synthesizer-styled HUD). The whole system needs a **user-friendly, intuitive UI usable by both the GM and the players** to manage changes — distinct from dialogue-management-panel, which is a GM-only live-session tool for DC'd critical conversations; this system is asynchronous, player-initiated, and needs its own player-facing surface, though the two may end up sharing components.
sourceContext: User's answer to an AskUserQuestion about Frame class assignment (frame-class-assignment in data/campaign/open-questions.json) — the direct question wasn't answered by pick; this system was offered instead as the real mechanism governing Frame/equipment change over time. Concretized further in a follow-up planning message, 2026-08-22, part of the same multi-part 'rant' that produced character-creation-intake-form.
openSubQuestions: How replies actually get authored in practice — now partially answered: pre-written dialogue-tree branches for anticipated paths, and an open ticket (Claude drafts a best-shot SF2E-legal implementation or one with interesting drawbacks, brought to the user for resolution) for anything free-typed outside those branches. Still open: who has final say when Claude's draft and the user's instinct disagree — presumably the user, but not stated.
Journal structure: one correspondence journal per kid, or one thread per in-fiction NPC relationship?

How 'negotiate new equipment' outcomes flow back into actual schema data — this needs to end up as a real inventory/loadout change on a frame.schema.json file, not just prose in a journal, so the sync path needs to cover that, not only text harvesting.

Whether this fully replaces the original frame-class-assignment question (verdict vs. player-chosen at creation) or sits alongside it — initial assignment and ongoing negotiated change could still be governed differently.
Exact dialogue-tree authoring format — a new lightweight schema, a reuse of challenge.schema.json's shape, or something bespoke to this system.
What 'semi-secure' means precisely for journal permissions.
How location-triggered writing actually surfaces in-session (a prompt on entering a scene? a persistent button tied to the Mimetic Controls panel? something else).
